turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what finally got me in here is... over these last few months, my mind just keeps jumping around. 

I drive a truck for a living, and lately, it's like every little thing pulls my attention away. Every time the CB radio chirps, or I pass a fuel price sign, or I just get some new idea in my head, I get completely sidetracked. And because of that, I'm starting to miss details that I normally never miss. Things like messing up a client’s delivery note or completely forgetting who I promised to call back. It's just starting to cause some real issues for me at work, so I figured I needed to come in.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient reports missing details and making careless mistakes, such as messing up a client's delivery note.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli like CB radio chirps, fuel price signs, and unrelated new ideas.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient mentions forgetting daily activities, specifically forgetting who they promised to call back.
symptom_reasoning.S039: The patient's attention is easily drawn to unimportant external stimuli (CB radio, signs) and internal ideas, causing them to get completely sidetracked.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: When you were a child, did you also have a hard time paying attention or staying focused?
turns.patient_response: No, not that I can remember. I mean, school was just school, but I never had any real trouble paying attention back then. I could sit still and get my work done just fine. This whole thing with my mind jumping around... it's really just been happening lately, like over the last few months.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient confirms current difficulties with paying attention and staying focused, noting that this is a recent issue unlike in their childhood.
symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient describes a recent subjective experience of their 'mind jumping around', indicative of racing thoughts.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a period when you felt unusually energized or wired, much more than your normal self?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, actually, I have. Lately, I've just been... going non-stop. I keep finding all these extra jobs for myself. Like, I'll spend hours rewriting my route plans to make them perfect, or I'll stay up late checking in on the new drivers after hours when I should be resting. And even when I get home, I'm fixing things around the house that don't even really need fixing right now. I just... I feel really antsy if I try to sit still for too long. It's like I have to keep moving.

symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient states they feel 'really antsy' if they try to sit still for too long.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes going 'non-stop' and feeling like they 'have to keep moving'.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient confirms feeling unusually energized, stating they have been going non-stop and finding extra jobs for themselves.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes a clear increase in goal-directed activities, such as rewriting route plans, checking on drivers, and fixing things around the house.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: During this time, have you been needing less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. Most nights lately, I'm only getting maybe three or four hours of sleep. And the weird thing is, I'm not even tired. I wake up before the sun's even out, and I just feel... ready to roll. Normally, running on that little sleep would have me completely worn out behind the wheel, but right now, I just get up and get going.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient explicitly confirms needing less sleep, stating they get only three or four hours a night but wake up feeling 'ready to roll' and not tired.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: During these past few months, have you felt unusually euphoric or unusually irritable compared with your normal self?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I'd say so. For months now, I've just been... I don't know, either way too fired up, like I'm on top of the world and everything's just gonna work out perfectly no matter what I do, or... or I'm just snapping at people. Like, over really small stuff at home or when I'm out working in the yard. It's just not my usual way of being. I'm normally a pretty even-keeled guy, but lately, it's just one extreme or the other.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient confirms experiencing both an elevated mood ('way too fired up, like I'm on top of the world') and an irritable mood ('snapping at people').
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient expresses inflated self-confidence, stating they feel 'everything's just gonna work out perfectly no matter what I do.'
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient describes reacting sharply to minor stimuli, specifically 'snapping at people... over really small stuff'.

turns.doctor_question: During this time, have you heard or seen things that other people said were not there?
turns.patient_response: No, I haven't had anything like that. I haven't seen or heard anything that wasn't there. It's just the energy and the mood stuff, really.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies seeing or hearing things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: Have you felt unusually powerful or important lately, like you could do things most people couldn’t?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I guess I have had some of that. Recently, I just... I got it in my head that I could rebuild the whole driver training program at work all by myself. I was convinced I could make it run way better than the bosses ever could. Which is funny looking back, because that’s not really my lane at all—I'm just a driver. But at the time, I really felt like I had all the answers and could just take over and fix everything they were doing wrong.

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient confirms feeling unusually capable and having all the answers, believing they could single-handedly rebuild the company's training program better than management.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any new medical illness or head injury around the time these symptoms started?
turns.patient_response: No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick with anything new, and... well, no, I definitely haven't hit my head or been in any accidents. Physically, I've been perfectly healthy.
